yearGuidance.1st: Learn one CAD tool properly and join an engineering society or competition team. Keep your first-year module marks; placement screeners ask for them.
yearGuidance.2nd: Placement-year applications open early in your second year. Write up your group design project with your part, the method and a result, and list relevant modules with marks.
yearGuidance.penultimate: Aim for a summer internship or a placement. Lead with your best design, build or test project, then your technical skills section.
yearGuidance.final: Graduate schemes look for one project you can explain in depth: your dissertation or final-year design project, with your part, the method and the result.
yearGuidance.masters: Put your MEng or MSc project first, with the tools and the technical result, and say if your degree is accredited (for example 'MEng, IMechE-accredited').

yearGuidance.1st: Keep a list of every technique you use in practicals, where, and whether you ran it yourself. Keep your first-year module marks; placement screeners ask for them.
yearGuidance.2nd: Placement-year applications at pharma and biotech firms open early in your second year. Lead with named techniques and one lab project with a result.
yearGuidance.penultimate: Aim for a summer studentship, a bursary-funded project or an industrial placement. Lead with your lab project and the techniques you ran independently.
yearGuidance.final: Graduate and lab roles look for your final-year project: the aim, the techniques, your part and the result. Show protocol and data discipline.
yearGuidance.masters: Put your research project first, with the techniques, the instruments and the result. For industry roles, keep publications after the project, not before.
